base: branch f5/wp5-6-utdf-hardening from main 953f567 (merge of PR #123, WP5.1)
question: Can the UTDF reader detect and report with a reason code the Doppler count problems RD-11 names (frozen counter with the validity flag set, counter rollover or reversal, a count discontinuity such as F2n's day-263 slip), check pad_xmit == pad_rcv, give correct elapsed time across a UTC leap second, and take the range-rate constants (transmit frequency, turnaround ratio K, count multiplier M) from the record, without moving any existing LRO study result?
rd_11: UTDF: the validity flag is unreliable on a frozen counter; pad_xmit is not checked (three-way record risk); leap-second crossing; hard-coded frequencies

conventions.time_tag: Bytes 11-18 are taken as a UTC calendar count: seconds of year = (day of year - 1) x 86400 + seconds of the UTC day, plus microseconds. This is the existing reader's convention, confirmed for 2009 by the archive file names (close time = last record + about 4 min). The handbook does not state how a leap second is counted. Consequences declared here: (1) at a year-end leap second, 23:59:60 Dec 31 encodes as seconds of year = days_in_year x 86400, a value no other instant can take, and is decoded as 23:59:60; (2) at a mid-year leap second (June 30) 23:59:60 encodes identically to 00:00:00 July 1 and cannot be told apart; a record there is decoded as 00:00:00 and a pair of records with the same tag is flagged TIME_NOT_INCREASING; (3) elapsed time between two records is the TAI difference, i.e. the UTC calendar difference plus the change of TAI - UTC, so an interval that straddles a leap second gains the extra SI second. The convention goes into docs/assurance/assumptions-and-limits.md
conventions.leap_table: TAI - UTC from 1972-01-01 (10 s) to 2017-01-01 (37 s), the 28 IERS steps, built into utdf.py so the reader stays SPICE-free; declared valid through 2026-06-30 (IERS Bulletin C: no leap second at the end of December 2025 or June 2026). Epochs after the horizon or before 1972 raise UTDFFormatError unless the caller passes its own tai_minus_utc function. The table is cross-checked against the repository's leapseconds kernel naif0012 (DELTET/DELTA_AT) when SPICE is available
conventions.range_rate: Handbook 4.2.2.4(c): rdot = -c [ (N_b - N_a)/(T_b - T_a) - 2.4e8 ] / (2 f_T K M), c = 299792458 m/s, f_T = the record's transmit frequency (10 Hz units), K and M from the record's frequency band (byte 52 high nibble): S-band (3) K = 240/221, M = 1000; VHF (1) K = 1, M = 1000; X-band (5) K = 880/749, M = 250. Other bands have no handbook constants: BAND_UNSUPPORTED and no range rate. The interval uses record a's frequency and requires record b's to be equal (else FREQUENCY_CHANGED)
conventions.counter: the bias-Doppler count is the 48-bit field of bytes 33-38, so it is a counter modulo 2^48

design.module: src/lunar_od/utdf.py, additive only. decode_record and read_utdf return the same field values as on main for every record; UTDFRecord gains raw fields with defaults appended last (band_byte = byte 52, tracking_mode = bytes 53-54) and properties: frequency_band, data_type, link_type (SRE mode bits 6-5: 1, 2, 3 or 0), turnaround_ratio and doppler_multiplier (None for an unsupported band), utc_iso (with :60 at a year-end leap second), tai_seconds_past_j2000. The existing utc property is unchanged except that a year-end leap-second record (which it cannot represent) raises UTDFFormatError instead of silently returning the next instant
design.record_check: record_reason_codes(record, *, file_pad=None) -> tuple of codes: PAD_XMIT_RCV_MISMATCH (pad_xmit != pad_rcv), PAD_FILE_MISMATCH (pad_rcv != the file name's PAD, when given), NOT_TWO_WAY (link_type != 2), BAND_UNSUPPORTED, MICROSECONDS_OUT_OF_RANGE (>= 1e6), SECONDS_OUT_OF_YEAR (beyond the year's length, a year-end leap second excepted). Empty tuple = clean
design.interval_check: check_doppler_counts(records, *, max_gap_s=60.0, max_range_rate_mps=3000.0, discontinuity_mps=0.020, window=4, file_pad=None, tai_minus_utc=None) -> list of DopplerInterval, one per consecutive pair of the given records in the given order whose both records are doppler_valid (the caller passes one station's stream, time-sorted, as F1c does). DopplerInterval: index_a, index_b, dt_s (TAI difference), dn (count difference, rollover-corrected), rate_hz, range_rate_mps (nan when not computable), codes. Interval codes: every record code of either end, then TIME_NOT_INCREASING (dt <= 0), GAP (dt > max_gap_s), FREQUENCY_CHANGED, COUNT_FROZEN (dn == 0), COUNT_ROLLOVER (raw dn < 0 and dn + 2^48 gives |rdot| <= max_range_rate_mps; dn is the corrected value and the interval is still flagged), COUNT_REVERSAL (raw dn < 0 otherwise), RATE_OUT_OF_RANGE (|rdot| > max_range_rate_mps, 3000 m/s = F2's MAX_DOPPLER_MPS), RATE_DISCONTINUITY. usable = no codes
design.discontinuity: Among intervals with no other code, split into runs at any interval that has a code: for each interval k, a least-squares cubic in the interval mid-time (TAI, centred, scaled) is fitted to up to `window` (4) unflagged neighbours on each side within the run, and the deviation d_k = rdot_k - prediction is formed; at least 6 neighbours are required, otherwise k is not tested (counted, reported as untested). Iteratively: the interval with the largest |d_k| above discontinuity_mps (0.020 m/s) is flagged RATE_DISCONTINUITY and removed from every neighbourhood, and all deviations are recomputed, until none exceeds it. Threshold reasoning before any number: F2n's slip is +1.024 m/s; per-interval count noise is ~0.5 mm/s (F2o robust sigma 0.44-0.59 mm/s), the cubic's prediction noise about 1.3x that, and its model error over 45 s of LRO dynamics ~1e-5 m/s; 20 mm/s is F2n's own 'big' line, ~30 prediction sigmas, so it is a counter-integrity check and not an outlier editor (F2o's residual editing stays the editor)
design.scripts: No study script is changed. The new functions are offered for WP5.4's frozen pipeline; adopting them in an existing study would be a re-freeze, which this WP does not do

gates.U_G2_REAL_SLIP: on fixture 1105, check_doppler_counts flags the interval starting 2009-09-20T11:03:15 with RATE_DISCONTINUITY and no other interval of the file with any code other than GAP (the file's contents beyond F2n's description were not looked at: F2n lists a 470 s gap ending near 11:02:10 and the station's 80 s gaps every 5 min); its |d_k| is within 5 % of F2n's 1.024 m/s residual
gates.U_G3_REAL_CONTROL: on fixture 0722 no interval has any code (false-alarm control)
gates.U_G4_ROLLOVER_FROZEN: synthetic streams built from the real 1105 records by rewriting only bytes 33-38: (a) counts shifted so the counter wraps 2^48 inside the stream: exactly the wrapping interval is COUNT_ROLLOVER, its corrected dn equals the unwrapped dn exactly, its range rate equals the unwrapped one bit for bit; (b) one record's count set equal to its predecessor's with the Doppler-valid flag kept: that interval is COUNT_FROZEN; (c) a count decrease not explained by a wrap: COUNT_REVERSAL; (d) an implied |rdot| > 3000 m/s: RATE_OUT_OF_RANGE; none of (a)-(d) is silently usable
gates.U_G5_PAD: synthetic records with pad_xmit != pad_rcv give PAD_XMIT_RCV_MISMATCH at record level and on both intervals that touch them; pad_xmit = 0 (the handbook's three-way S-band value) is a mismatch; a record whose pad_rcv differs from file_pad gives PAD_FILE_MISMATCH; link_type 3 gives NOT_TWO_WAY
gates.U_G6_LEAP_SECOND: test_utdf_leap_second_crossing: (a) a 5 s synthetic stream 2016-12-31T23:59:50 ... 2017-01-01T00:00:10 including the year-end leap record (year 16, seconds of year 366 x 86400): utc_iso gives 2016-12-31T23:59:60.000000 for it, tai_seconds_past_j2000 increases by exactly 5 s (or 1 s into and out of the leap record) as the SI time does, the interval 23:59:55 -> 00:00:00 when the leap record is absent has dt_s = 6 s exactly, and its range rate uses 6 s; utc on the leap record raises UTDFFormatError; (b) June 30 2015: 23:59:55 -> 2015-07-01T00:00:00 has dt_s = 6 s; two records tagged 00:00:00 give TIME_NOT_INCREASING; (c) an interval with no leap second has dt_s equal to the datetime difference exactly; (d) tai_seconds_past_j2000 equals SPICE's (str2et of the UTC string minus 32.184 s minus TDB-TT) only through the table: the built-in table equals naif0012's DELTET/DELTA_AT at every step (spice test; skipped only when the kernel is absent, the skip reported); (e) an epoch after 2026-06-30 raises unless tai_minus_utc is given
gates.U_G7_RECORD_FREQUENCIES: (a) range_rate_mps for S, VHF and X-band synthetic records equals the handbook formula with that band's K and M and the record's f_T; a band without constants gives BAND_UNSUPPORTED and nan; a transmit frequency change between the two records gives FREQUENCY_CHANGED. (b) On all development-day Doppler intervals formed as F1c forms them (doppler_valid, same PAD, 0 < dt <= 60 s, records sorted by PAD and time), the new range_rate_mps equals F1c's expression -C (dn/dt - BIAS_HZ) / (2 f_T TURNAROUND M_MULT) to <= 4 ulp relative (2 x DBL_EPSILON x 2), i.e. the record-derived K, M and the TAI dt reproduce the constants the studies used (2009 has no leap second; every record is S-band)
gates.U_G8_RESULTS_DO_NOT_MOVE: (a) for every record of the five development days, decode_record on this branch returns the same values in every field main's UTDFRecord has, and read_utdf the same records (main's utdf.py loaded from git show 953f567:src/lunar_od/utdf.py); (b) no file under studies/phase17/scripts, studies/phase17/results or src/lunar_od other than utdf.py changes; (c) impact as computed, information and reported in full: per development day, the F1c-formed Doppler intervals that check_doppler_counts flags, by code, with each RATE_DISCONTINUITY listed with its UTC and |d_k|, and whether it is among F2o's edited intervals. Expectation, not a gate: the F2n slip on 263; no COUNT_FROZEN among doppler_valid intervals; a few or no other discontinuities. A flagged interval does not move any study result because no study script calls the new check

expectations: stated before the run, not gates: U_G2 d_k ~ +1.02 m/s (sign: the slip leaves the count short, rate low, rdot high); U_G3 0 codes; U_G7(b) exact equality on most intervals (the same operations in a different association may differ by 1-2 ulp); U_G8(c) on 263 one RATE_DISCONTINUITY (the slip), perhaps 0-3 elsewhere at 20 mm/s; F2o's 7 + 4 + ... edited intervals are mostly below 20 mm/s and not flagged
out_of_scope: a sample-rate check against bytes 53-54 (the field reads 1 s on PADs 103-129 while records are 5 s apart, so its meaning is not settled; decoded and exposed only), angle decoding, AGC, three-way processing (flagged, not processed), adopting the checks in existing studies (would be a re-freeze), the DSN TRK-2-34 reader (WP5.5/WP6.3), and the WP5.4 hold-out run
reject_if: if a gate fails, WP5.6 is reported as computed and not offered for merge until a fix passes a gate set recorded in docs/assurance/amendment-log.md; a change to a gate or threshold after its result is exploratory
agent_decisions: agent decisions under the owner's delegation, flagged for review: (1) the UTC calendar time-tag convention and the mid-year leap-second ambiguity declared rather than guessed away; (2) a built-in leap table with a horizon instead of a SPICE dependency in the reader; (3) the 20 mm/s discontinuity threshold and the cubic leave-out predictor, a counter-integrity check that leaves F2o editing in place; (4) flagged intervals are returned, not dropped, so a caller sees every code; (5) existing studies are not switched to the new checks (no re-freeze); (6) two real archived files (7.2 kB, public PDS data) committed as test fixtures
